title: List uncited interventions as open work in athena status
summary: `athena status` counts interventions but never lists them as open work. The fix lists each intervention that no later job cites under open work, with a next command in `next`. The audience is a fresh-context user or agent who should not have to read the records to find follow-ups (m6 in the v0 acceptance review).

defaults_applied.how: New unit and integration tests; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria check that status lists and then drops the intervention, not that fields exist.
One focused change to status computation and rendering.
The status view derives open interventions from the records, not from a single instance.
Behavior criteria name the cargo commands the verifier can run.
Recovered the citation meaning and the next command from the repository and the review.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: An intervention is 'cited' when a request job created after it names its record id in the request text. Records have no dedicated citing field, so the producer should check for a better existing link, such as the job or introspection fields, and use it if one exists.
Every intervention without such a citation counts as needing follow-up. The producer may exclude cases the repository shows are already handled.
The next command is `athena ask "<request that addresses intervention ID>"`. `athena ask` exists in the CLI, but the producer should confirm its argument form.

The change is in `StatusView` and `status()` in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs, and in the text rendering in crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs. Interventions are listed in the status output, not added to the job `open` list.
The goal is the acceptance review's m6 fix. The JSON status shape gains an additive field.
The `tested` default needs a unit test for a cited intervention and an uncited one, plus a CLI integration test.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test`. A new test records an intervention against a landed job and shows `athena status` listing it as open work, with its id, category and a next command. A second new test shows it disappears from open work once a later job's request cites its id.
The status view has a distinct open-interventions list (id, what, category, next command). Its entries also appear in `next`, so a reader sees what to run without opening records.
An intervention cited by a later job is not listed. The rule for 'cited' is documented in a doc comment and in docs where status is described.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean.
The existing counts under 'interventions' (by category and class) are unchanged. Status for a repository with no interventions shows no new open work.

out_of_scope: Fixing the other findings in the acceptance review (m1–m5, m7 and later).
Changing the intervention record schema or adding new record types.
departures: The meaning of 'cites' is under-specified, since records have no dedicated citing field. That makes acceptance and verification slightly less likely than the reference.
